objectives: Read short controlled text with increasing accuracy.
concepts: Words can share a rime while their onset changes.
Word-family recognition supports pattern efficiency but does not replace full-word decoding.
Controlled rereading strengthens accurate connected reading.

definitions.definition: A group of words that share the same rime pattern.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable.
The initial consonant or consonant group before the rime.

commonMistakes: Reading only the rime and ignoring the onset.
Treating all family members as identical words.
Guessing from the family instead of decoding.

basic: Sort /r/ words into common rime families.
conceptual: Explain how the onset changes while the rime stays constant.
application: Read controlled /r/ word-family sentences and identify pattern evidence.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why family recognition still requires complete word decoding.
mixedReview: Mix /r/ families with previously learned CVC patterns.

quickRevision: find onset → find rime → blend → reread
mistakeBasedRevision: If the learner guesses from the family, return to phoneme-by-phoneme blending.
weakTopicRevision: Practice the weakest rime family using fresh controlled words.

outcomes: Learner decodes complete words using onset and rime.
Learner reads controlled /r/ text with improving accuracy.

questions.question: Why does word-family practice help early reading?
options: It highlights recurring rime patterns while still supporting full-word decoding

options: Target -ug decoding and controlled rereading with fresh words
